topic: Zanzibar-style relationship-based access control (ReBAC) systems and fit for meept (single-daemon, pure-Go, SQLite-backed, no external services)

verification_notes.zanzibar_leap: UNVERIFIED: targeted searches for a technique called 'Zanzibar Leap' returned no hits. The verified consistency concepts from the paper are: zookies (opaque consistency tokens), external consistency, snapshot reads with bounded staleness, and the 'new enemy' problem. If 'Zanzibar leap' was meant as a specific follow-up technique, it could not be confirmed and is intentionally not described.
verification_notes.method: Facts below are drawn from USENIX paper text, GitHub repo metadata, pkg.go.dev, CNCF project pages, and project blogs returned by web_search; each entry carries cited URLs.

options.name: Google Zanzibar (reference paper)
options.what_it_is: Google's globally distributed ACL storage and evaluation system (USENIX ATC 2019), backing Drive, Calendar, Cloud IAM, Photos, YouTube.
key_ideas: Relation tuples: object#relation@subject; subjects can be usersets (nested groups), enabling object-to-object relations like doc:readme#parent@folder:A
Namespace configs with userset rewrite rules (union/intersection/exclusion) define derived permissions (viewer contains editor contains owner)
APIs: Check, Expand (effective userset tree), Read, Write, Watch
Consistency: external consistency via Spanner TrueTime timestamps; zookie tokens bound snapshot staleness; prevents the 'new enemy' problem (revoked user must not see new content via stale ACLs)
Scale framing: 2+ trillion ACLs, millions of checks/sec, <10ms p95, 99.999% availability
options.zanzibar_leap: Not verifiable in this research pass - see verification_notes.
options.fit_for_meept: The DATA MODEL (tuples + inheritance graph walk) is a great fit for 'agent -> group -> resource' checks; the DISTRIBUTED CONSISTENCY machinery (Spanner, zookies, multi-region) is unnecessary overhead for a single SQLite-backed daemon, where serialized SQLite transactions already give external consistency for free.

options.name: OpenFGA
options.type: authorization server, embeddable as a Go library
options.maturity: High and growing: CNCF Sandbox Sep 2022, moved to CNCF Incubating Oct 28 2025; ~5.9k GitHub stars; created by Auth0/Okta engineers; production adopters include Grafana Labs, Canonical, Docker, Agicap; v1.22.x on pkg.go.dev.
options.go_integration: Dual story. (1) Standalone server (`openfga run`) over HTTP/gRPC, usually with PostgreSQL/MySQL (SQLite adapter is beta). (2) Library embedding: `pkg/server` `NewServerWithOpts(...)` with any implementation of the `pkg/storage.OpenFGADatastore` interface, including the built-in in-memory datastore; the README explicitly advertises 'Can also be embedded as a Go library'. Maintainers have confirmed embedding works with no network when the datastore is local.
embeddability_caveats: Historically request validation lived in gRPC middleware, so library users lost it - fixed by moving validation into the RPC methods (issue #965 closed via PR #975 / #2670)
Issue #1874 (still OPEN as of research date): some server-config validations still don't run when used as a library
Internal graph-resolution code stays in `internal/` - you embed the Server struct, not the raw graph engine
options.data_model_fit: Native fit: types + relations + conditions model 'agent belongs to group, group has viewer on resource, check(agent, viewer, resource)' directly; supports contextual/conditional tuples (ABAC-lite).
options.operational_cost: As a server: one more process + datastore to run (violates meept's no-external-services constraint unless embedded). Embedded: pure Go dependency, in-memory datastore or a custom SQLite-backed OpenFGADatastore implementation; dependency footprint is non-trivial (gRPC, protobuf, otel) but contained in-process.
options.fit_verdict: BEST candidate among the big three for meept's constraint: Apache-2.0, CNCF-governed, SQLite-capable, and genuinely embeddable. Risk: embedding is a second-class path (open validation bugs, `internal/` boundaries), so it must be validated with a spike before committing.

options.name: SpiceDB
options.maturity: Highest among OSS Zanzibar implementations ('most mature' per its own docs, battle-tested since 2021 by AuthZed); ~7.1k stars; actively released (v1.57.0 at research time).
options.go_integration: Standard deployment is a SEPARATE SpiceDB server plus an external datastore: PostgreSQL (recommended single-region), CockroachDB (recommended multi-region), Spanner, MySQL (not recommended); memdb only for dev/test. Go client is authzed/authzed-go over gRPC. Partial library story: a `pkg/embedded` package now exists that runs SpiceDB's permission engine in-process (no gRPC), but it exposes ONLY `CheckPermission` (no schema/relationship writes API surface, no watch/lookup) and still requires constructing a `datastore.Datastore`; checks are always evaluated at head revision.
options.data_model_fit: Excellent: schema language (zed) with definitions, relations, permissions; subjects can be `agent`, `group#member`, wildcards; caveats for conditional access.
options.operational_cost: High for meept: a dedicated server process plus Postgres/CockroachDB is exactly the heavyweight external service meept excludes. Embedded `pkg/embedded` mode avoids the second process but is check-only and leans on a datastore implementation you'd have to write against SQLite.
options.fit_verdict: Poor fit for single-daemon meept despite being the most mature option: server+datastore in the normal path; embedded mode too narrow to be the primary integration. Would only make sense if meept ever grew a dedicated multi-service authz tier.

options.name: Permify
options.license: AGPL-3.0 since May 13 2025 (was Apache-2.0 before; license swap via PR #2228) - copyleft matters for anything linking/embedding it
options.maturity: ACTIVE, not archived: acquired by FusionAuth on Nov 20 2025 with a public commitment to stay open source; steady release cadence since (v1.6.x through v1.7.5, Oct 2026; commits into Oct 2026); ~5.9-6.1k stars.
options.go_integration: Server-first: runs as `permify` server (gRPC/HTTP/REST) backed primarily by PostgreSQL; consumed via generated SDKs. No documented embed-as-a-Go-library path surfaced in this research (its engine packages live under `internal/`, implying import restrictions) - treat as server-only.
options.data_model_fit: Good on paper (schema + relationships + permission checks, Zanzibar-inspired, multi-tenancy).
options.operational_cost: Separate server + Postgres. AGPL-3.0 is the decisive blocker: linking it into a distributed single-binary daemon triggers network-copyleft obligations.
options.fit_verdict: Poor fit: server+Postgres violates the no-external-services constraint, and AGPL-3.0 makes embedding legally unattractive for a self-hosted platform binary. Note the license was Apache before May 2025 - old pins/forks may silently differ.

options.name: Embeddable Zanzibar-style Go libraries
sourcenetwork/zanzi
options.detail: 'Zanzibar based ReBAC embeddable authorization engine', pure Go, has a documented embedded-library usage example (example/embedded) plus gRPC mode. Last push 2026-05-14. BUT: 7 stars, 2 contributors - tiny bus factor, essentially a two-person project. License not confirmed in this pass.

options.name: xraph/warden
options.detail: In-process Go engine combining RBAC + ABAC + ReBAC ('Zanzibar-style relation tuples and a graph walk, inside your own process and database. There is no separate authorization service to run' - direct quote from README). Apache-2.0, works against PostgreSQL/SQLite/MongoDB/in-memory, v1.8.x on pkg.go.dev, releases into late 2026. BUT: repo created 2026-02-20 with ~1 star - very young, unproven adoption.

options.name: trevex/zanzigo
options.detail: Minimal building-blocks library for a Zanzibar-esque resolver (model + tuple store + Check); useful as a reference implementation more than a dependency; tiny project.

options.name: atol.sh/sdk-go
options.detail: Embeds Zanzibar relationship checks in-process, BUT bootstraps model/tuples from the atol.sh SaaS at startup - external service dependency, disqualified for meept.

options.note: No large, battle-tested pure-library Zanzibar implementation exists in Go. The embeddable options are all small-community projects; the mature systems (OpenFGA, SpiceDB, Permify) are all server-first with library embedding as a secondary path.

overall_recommendation_for_meept.summary: Adopt the Zanzibar DATA MODEL, not a Zanzibar SYSTEM. Meept's 'agent -> group -> resource' checks map naturally onto relation tuples, but every mature Zanzibar-style system is built for distributed, multi-service deployments and conflicts with meept's no-external-services constraint.
ranked_options: 1. Roll a minimal ReBAC engine in-repo: a relation-tuples table in meept's existing SQLite store (`object_type:object_id#relation@subject`, subjects may be usersets) plus a bounded recursive userset-resolution Check with a cycle guard. This is a few hundred lines, keeps data co-located with session/employee storage, and needs no zookies - a single SQLite writer gives external consistency by construction.

2. Embed OpenFGA as a Go library (Apache-2.0, CNCF Incubating, SQLite-beta adapter, documented `NewServerWithOpts` + in-memory datastore path) with a custom SQLite-backed `OpenFGADatastore`. Viable but must be spike-validated: library mode has known open validation gaps (issue #1874) and a heavy dependency footprint (gRPC/otel).
3. Avoid SpiceDB (server+datastore required; embedded pkg/embedded is Check-only) and Permify (server+Postgres, AGPL-3.0).
overall_recommendation_for_meept.when_to_revisit: If meept grows optional clustering with cross-node authz decisions, revisiting OpenFGA (server or embedded) becomes worthwhile; the tuple schema from option 1 is OpenFGA-model-compatible, keeping a migration path open.
